cohort: The study analyzed European fertility and cesarean section data for 2015 and followed a cohort of Slovak women who gave birth for the first time in 2006.
finding: A 10% increase in cesarean section frequency across European countries corresponded to a 0.102 drop in fertility rate, and a first delivery by cesarean section significantly reduced the probability of a subsequent delivery (OR=0.68) for individual women.
mod_finding: First delivery by cesarean section significantly lowered the probability of a second delivery (OR=0.68), with the most notable impact observed in women aged 26-30 years (OR=0.66) and those with higher education (OR=0.58).
